results.comment: At around 4:00 John responds to Murray's claim that he "had no opportunity to defend himself" by stating it's "not how anything works". He's correct. Day One of a journalism degree is learning about the inverted pyramid.   Day Two (and many other days thereafter) is learning the fundamental practice of seeking comment from the subject/s of your reporting. It's not just about fairness, although fairness is a significant component. It's also about balance. Even 'he said, she said' shows the attempt to get both sides. And when you see 'could not be reached for comment' or 'declined our requests for comment/an interview', you know that the effort has been made.  In Murray's case, LWT contacted Murray Energy for comment about the story they were producing. Murray Energy responded with a 'cease and desist' letter, their attempt to force LWT/HBO to abandon the story. They didn't, as we know, so Murray, a man with acres of thin skin, filed a defamation lawsuit. On a side note, the ACLU filed an amicus brief (amicus briefs are filed by people/organizations not party in a suit, but with an interest in a case).  The "opportunity to defend" himself came long before the story aired. LWT sought comment. It's about as simple and clear as can be. Eat shit, Bob.
